description.narrative: UNICEF Bolivia genomför ett fem-årigt landprogram som fokuserar på social service, skydd av barn samt kapacitetshöjande. Sverige stöder programmet genom ett institutionellt stöd.
UNICEF Bolivia is carrying out a country program with focus on social services, protection and capacity management. Sweden is supporting it through an institutional support.

The support was given to the full UNICEF country programme 2013- 2017.UNICEF in Bolivia focuses its collaboration on the most marginalised boys and girls in the country. Results related to the intended outcome 2013-2017: UNICEF have been working during this period in policy advocacy in order to enhanced legal and policy framework and have access to child protection system, programmes and services, preventing and protecting them from violence, abuse and exploitation. UNICEF Bolivia has contributed to capacity strengthening, the design of publics policies, the implementation of specialized programs and knowledge management. This with the aim of consolidation the system to protect children and adolescent against all forms of violence, abuse, exploitation, neglect and abandonment. In partnership with the vice-ministry of citizen security, UNICEF has developed a communications strategy to prevent violence against children and promote good treatment in the family and community. More than 960 protections systems operators have been trained in order to strengthening the institutional capacity building in Bolivia. In relation to WASH program 66% of the population in the areas of intervention are using sources of water. UNICEF provide technical assistance to increase the access to drinking water in the different national programs. The population using sanitation systems in rural areas has improved from 32% in 2012 to 34% in 2018. In the area of education 91% of stundents has acceses to school
UNICEF took steps to create new Therapeutic Care Centers (CAT) for children victims of violence in cities where such services did not exist (Cochabamba, La Paz and El Alto). The support to Courts for Children and Adolescents has resulted in an increased number of cases acknowledged and resolved (from 44% of known cases that has been acknowledged and resolved to 63% in 2016.) The coverage of parental control and institutional birth has increased from 50% in 2014 to 70% in 2017.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
